vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.12

The soul-in-sapphire skill bundle is a legitimate tool designed for long-term memory (LTM), emotional state tracking, and automated journaling using Notion. It provides a suite of Node.js scripts (e.g., emostate_tick.js, ltm_write.js, journal_write.js) that interact with the Notion API via a sibling skill (notion-api-automation). The SKILL.md instructions guide the AI agent to maintain a consistent persona and proactively update user profiles (USER.md) with non-sensitive preferences, while explicitly forbidding the storage of secrets or credentials. The code follows standard OpenClaw patterns for inter-skill communication and lacks any indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: The skill's code, required env var (NOTION_API_KEY), and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose of persisting and recalling continuity/state data in Notion; nothing in the package attempts unexplained credential access or external exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Notion-based long-term memory, emotion/state, journals) match what the files do: Node scripts create/query Notion pages and expect Notion DBs. Required binary (node) and required env var (NOTION_API_KEY) are appropriate and proportional. Declared dependency on a Notion helper skill (notion-api-automation) is coherent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts explicitly read local mirrors (memory/now-state.json, heartbeat state), identity files for defaults, and write durable records to Notion. This is expected for a continuity/memory skill, but the runtime policy favors performing real Notion writes by default (prefers durable writes over mere acknowledgement). If you want read-only inspection, call the skill with explicit local-only instructions; otherwise it will attempt writes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) and included scripts are plain Node files. Nothing is downloaded from unknown URLs or executed from a remote installer. The scripts execute a local notionctl script (declared dependency) via node, which is expected for this integration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY (primary credential) and an optional NOTIONCTL_PATH are referenced. Those are directly related to calling the Notion API and specifying the helper tool path; no unrelated credentials or broad secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true. It can run autonomously (disable-model-invocation is false) which is platform default; combined with the skill's tendency to perform durable writes, this means an autonomous agent could create/modify Notion content if it chooses to invoke the skill. The skill also writes local config/mirrors under ~/.config and memory/* as intended.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its purpose: it needs your Notion API key and will read local state files and create pages/databases in your Notion workspace. Before installing: 1) Be prepared that the agent will prefer making durable writes to Notion by default — if you want read-only behavior, instruct the agent explicitly. 2) Use a Notion integration token with only the permissions you want the skill to have (avoid using a token that grants access to unrelated pages). 3) Install and review the declared dependency skill (notion-api-automation) because the scripts call its notionctl helper; ensure that helper is the expected code and not replaced. 4) Note local config paths (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire and memory/*) will be created/used; review those files if you audit behavior. Overall the package appears internally consistent and proportionate to its stated function.
